passage: At the village anganwadi, two-year-old Harsha sees little Suraj crying over a dropped roti. She toddles over and pats his back, pat-pat, the way her Ajji does. When the helper asks her to pass the cups, she carries them one by one, beaming. Then Suraj reaches for her wooden bullock. Harsha hands it over at once. But she keeps staring at it, thumb in mouth. Ajji notices. "Harsha, do you want it back?" Harsha nods, very small.

qa.q: What does Harsha hand over to Suraj?
qa.a: She hands over her wooden bullock.

qa.q: What does Harsha staring at the bullock with her thumb in her mouth suggest she is feeling?
qa.a: She seems torn and a little sad, wanting her bullock back even though she gave it away so readily.

qa.q: What choice did Ajji make on noticing Harsha's stare?
qa.a: Ajji gently asked if she wanted it back, giving her unspoken wish a voice.

qa.q: How might Suraj feel when Harsha pats his back?
qa.a: He probably feels comforted and less alone with his dropped roti.

grounding: A warm toddler comforts a crying child, follows requests happily and gives up her toy, while her grandmother notices an unspoken want.

passage: At the playground in Utrecht, Esther, two and a half, gives her red spade to Noa before he even asks. When Noa falls and wails, she squats down and strokes his arm. "Sorry, sorry." When her Oma says, "Shoes on, please," Esther sits to try at once. Later Noa climbs into the baby swing Esther was waiting for. She stands very still beside it, lip wobbling, saying nothing. Oma kneels. "Esther, is it your turn next?" Esther nods and grips Oma's hand.

qa.q: What does Esther give to Noa?
qa.a: She gives Noa her red spade.

qa.q: What is Esther feeling as she stands still by the swing, lip wobbling?
qa.a: She feels sad and wants her turn, but she doesn't say so.

qa.q: What choice did Oma make when Esther stood silently by the swing?
qa.a: Oma knelt and asked if it was her turn next, helping her show the want she hadn't spoken.

qa.q: How might Noa feel when Esther strokes his arm after his fall?
qa.a: He likely feels comforted and cared for by his playmate.

grounding: A toddler shares, comforts a hurt playmate and follows requests readily, but hides her own want until her grandmother asks.

passage:
'Harish is crying, Joseph. His truck broke.'
Joseph looked at his own red truck, then toddled over and pushed it into Harish's hands. He patted Harish's head. 'There. There.'
'That's kind, kanna,' said Amma. 'Can you bring me the spoon?'
Joseph fetched it, beaming.
Later Amma saw him watching Harish zoom the red truck, his thumb in his mouth.
'Joseph, did you want to keep your truck?'
Joseph's chin wobbled. 'Mine. Also.'
'Then after lunch it comes back to you.'

qa.q: What did Joseph give Harish?
qa.a: His red truck.

qa.q: What does Joseph's thumb in his mouth, watching Harish, suggest?
qa.a: He may be feeling a little sad and missing his truck, a want he didn't say out loud.

qa.q: Why was Amma's question a good idea?
qa.a: It let Joseph say he wanted his truck too, so his kindness didn't hide his own wish, and a turn after lunch made it fair.

qa.q: How might Harish feel when Joseph pats his head?
qa.a: Harish probably feels comforted, getting a truck and a pat just when his own toy broke.

grounding: Shows a toddler who warmly hands over a toy, comforts a crying child and follows requests, while hiding a want an adult asks about.

passage:
Note for Omkar's parents
Omkar was our little helper today. When Tia cried for her mother, he brought her his blanket and patted her back. He put the blocks away when asked. At snack he gave his biscuit to Rayan. Ten minutes later I found him by the window, eyes wet. I asked, 'Did you want your biscuit?' He nodded. We shared mine. He gives so quickly that he may not say what he wants, so I'll keep checking.
Afreen, caregiver

qa.q: What did Omkar bring Tia?
qa.a: His blanket.

qa.q: Why were Omkar's eyes wet by the window?
qa.a: He was sad about giving away his biscuit; he had wanted it but hadn't said so.

qa.q: What is Afreen's plan, and why does it matter?
qa.a: To keep checking what Omkar wants, because he gives so quickly that his own wishes can go unspoken.

qa.q: How might Omkar's parents feel reading this note?
qa.a: Proud of his kindness, and glad the caregiver noticed his hidden want and gently asked.

grounding: Shows, in a caregiver's note, a toddler who comforts and shares readily and follows requests, but hides his own want until an adult asks.

passage: At the village feast in Goa, Francis followed his mother Sarita everywhere, proudly carrying her basket of bananas when she asked. When a little girl dropped her sweet in the dust and wailed, Francis toddled over and held out his own. Then he stood by the rope swing, watching the bigger children, not asking. Sarita crouched. 'Do you want a turn, baba?' He nodded hard. She lifted him on and pushed him gently.

qa.q: What did Francis carry for Sarita?
qa.a: Her basket of bananas.

qa.q: What does Francis standing by the swing, not asking, suggest?
qa.a: He wanted a turn but stayed quiet, perhaps shy, so his wish was hidden.

qa.q: What did Sarita's question do for Francis?
qa.a: It brought out the want he hadn't said, so he got his turn on the swing.

qa.q: How might the little girl feel when Francis holds out his sweet?
qa.a: She would likely feel comforted and surprised, her tears easing at an unexpected kindness.

grounding: Shows a toddler who happily follows requests and comforts a crying child, while a quiet want goes unspoken until his mother asks.

passage: At the playgroup in Bergen, Ingrid, two, saw Esther crying by the swings. She toddled over, patted Esther's arm and held out her own rice cake. When the teacher said, "Tidy-up time!" Ingrid happily carried the blocks. But the teacher noticed Ingrid always let others take the swing first. She knelt. "Ingrid, do you want a turn too?" Ingrid looked at the swing, then nodded hard.

qa.q: What did Ingrid offer Esther?
qa.a: Her own rice cake.

qa.q: What does Ingrid's nod suggest about her wants?
qa.a: It suggests she really wanted a turn on the swing but was too eager to please to ask.

qa.q: What did the teacher do that was wise?
qa.a: The teacher noticed Ingrid always gave way and gently asked about her own wish.

qa.q: How might Esther have felt when Ingrid patted her arm?
qa.a: Esther may have felt comforted and less alone.

grounding: Shows a toddler who comforts a peer, shares and follows requests happily, and an adult asking about the unspoken wants her warmth can hide.
